passage: The Mensah group compared two receptor proteins, A and B, that bind a cofactor mimic with different affinities. Purified protein was held at 1 nM, a concentration far below either dissociation constant, so that the free ligand concentration was approximately equal to the total added. Ligand was titrated over a wide range, and the fraction of protein with bound ligand was measured by fluorescence anisotropy after each addition reached equilibrium. Each binding curve was hyperbolic and showed no evidence of cooperativity. The researchers intend to use the receptor with the tighter binding as a biosensor, and they want to know what ligand concentration would be required to saturate it at 80% occupancy. All measurements were made at 25 °C in identical buffer. Protein stocks were centrifuged before use to remove aggregates, and ligand stocks were verified by absorbance. All procedures followed the laboratory's standard operating protocols, and raw data were archived before analysis.

questions.stem: At [ligand] = 100 nM, what is the fraction of protein A bound?
questions.explanation: Fraction bound = [L]/(Kd + [L]) = 100/(10+100) = 0.91. The B column gives 0.5.
questions.trap: Reading the protein B column (0.5) or the 50 nM row (0.83) instead of the 100 nM row of the protein A column.

questions.stem: Why was protein held far below the Kd?

options.A: So that the protein is certain to be fully saturated
options.B: So that Kd equals the protein concentration
options.C: So that cooperativity can be detected
options.D: So that ligand depletion by binding is negligible and free ligand ≈ total ligand

questions.explanation: If protein were comparable to Kd, binding would deplete free ligand and distort the fit to the simple hyperbola.
questions.trap: Thinking the very low protein concentration is meant to saturate the protein or to make Kd equal the protein concentration, rather than to keep ligand depletion negligible.

questions.stem: What ligand concentration is needed for 80% occupancy of the higher-affinity protein (Kd = 10 nM)?
questions.trap: Taking [L] equal to Kd (10 nM) as 80% occupancy, when that gives only 50%; 80% needs four times Kd.

options.A: Kd equals the ligand concentration at half-saturation
options.B: A lower Kd means lower affinity
options.C: Protein A binds the ligand with higher affinity than protein B
options.D: A hyperbolic curve is consistent with noncooperative binding

questions.explanation: Kd is inversely related to affinity: a smaller Kd means tighter binding.
questions.trap: Confusing Kd with an association constant and treating a lower Kd as weaker binding, when a lower Kd means tighter binding.

questions.stem: Which protein behavior differs from these hyperbolic curves?

options.A: Binding of a single ligand to one site on a monomeric protein
options.C: Hemoglobin's sigmoidal oxygen binding due to cooperativity

questions.explanation: Hemoglobin binds O₂ cooperatively (Hill coefficient > 1), giving a sigmoidal curve, while myoglobin is hyperbolic like proteins A and B.
questions.trap: Choosing a one-site monomer or a Michaelis–Menten curve because they sound unusual, when both are hyperbolic and only cooperative hemoglobin binding is sigmoidal.
